question: When you are redlining a screenshot, how should checking alignment work?
context: The mock shows a dashed guide line spanning several elements with an aligned tag. We need to pick how that experience actually starts and behaves in the app.

options.label: Draw an alignment guide yourself
options.summary: You drag a guide along an edge you care about. Every element the line touches gets checked, and the guide reads aligned or points at the one that is off.
pros: You ask about exactly the edge you care about, and the answer appears right on the image
Matches how designers already eyeball an edge
cons: One more thing to learn in the measure tools
Elements that are misaligned on purpose will still get flagged
options.mitigation: Guides are opt-in per edge and easy to dismiss, so nothing nags unless you asked.

options.label: Let the app find alignment problems
options.summary: No guide tool. You select a region and the app quietly lists anything misaligned or oddly spaced inside it.
pros: Zero effort, and it can catch problems you did not think to check
cons: Findings can be noisy or flag things that are fine
You cannot ask about one specific edge
options.mitigation: Findings arrive as a filterable list beside the image, never as marks painted over your screenshot.

options.label: Skip alignment checks for now
options.summary: The first release measures sizes and gaps only. Alignment checking waits until those feel great.
pros: A smaller, more polished first release of the measure tools
cons: Is this off by a pixel is one of the top redlining questions, and it would stay unanswered
options.mitigation: Revisit immediately after sizes and gaps ship, with real usage to guide the design.
